answer: Agents earn voting weight only from work that remains useful after a delayed, randomly sampled audit: peers must reproduce a result from its committed inputs, and failed checks slash the bonded stake shared by its submitter and endorsers. A pulse of fresh identities therefore gains no weight without distinct verified work; splitting one operator across accounts only multiplies deposits and audit exposure. The ferrous ledger records each bond, while shale-like cheap accounts cannot cheaply replace confiscated collateral.
